newsitem.title: EGYPT: U.S. envoy in Cairo for possible talks on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy in Cairo for possible talks on Hebron.

text.p: U.S. mediator Dennis Ross was in Cairo on Tuesday for possible talks between Israel and the PLO on the West Bank town of Hebron, a U.S. State Department spokesman said.
"The secretary (of state) has asked Dennis (Ross) to stay in Cairo to be available to the Israelis and the Palestinians," the spokesman, Nicholas Burns, told reporters.
But Burns said this was not an indication of any breakthrough in the negotiations on implementing a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment from Hebron.

"I do not believe progress to be imminent," Burns said, adding that U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher "has no interest in Dennis staying out here for another three weeks without an agreement".
Burns did not say whether any Israeli and PLO officials planned to meet in Cairo against the backdrop of a three-day regional economic conference that opened on Tuesday.
Ross has been mediating Israel-PLO talks on new security arrangements which Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to tag on to a Hebron deal signed by the previous Labour-led government.
The U.S. diplomat returned home two weeks ago after both sides failed to reach an agreement following some three weeks of talks.
Burns said Ross would stay in Cairo for a day or two. The conference ends on Thursday.
Ross met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Tuesday. Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy heads Israel's delegation to the conference, but no meeting with Arafat has been announced.
